importantFindings.title: A heading with a short non-keyword prefix before its date can still produce a ready false row
importantFindings.finding: The S4-DI-16 fix works for lines that start with a date: the three new it.each cases and my earlier date-first probes give 0 extra rows. The rule is now 'judge the whole line only when no letter precedes the first date'. So a heading whose prefix has only a particle or an abbreviation before the date, and its keyword after the date, still passes the keyword test. I ran the codex/0.3.0 and HEAD parsers on the same text-only page with 9 invented headings and footers. The base parser gives 0 extra rows. HEAD gives 5 extra rows; 4 are headings and 1 is the student row with trailing grid noise that the base parser wrongly drops. Two of the headings are complete and ready under the screen rules: a particle before the date, and an abbreviation plus a number plus a particle before the date. Neither case appeared on the five captures or in 80 perturbed runs. The case is narrower than the student drop it replaced.
importantFindings.recommendation: Judge the whole line when the leading text has no non-particle word of 3 or more letters, and add those two shapes to the it.each tests. This is not blocking because it was never observed and every row stays visible.

importantFindings.title: Published history still carries real student data; the owner has deferred the fix
importantFindings.finding: The current tree is clean. My independent per-word scan (surname words on their own, each surname word next to the same student's given-name words, multi-word given names, birth dates in four formats) finds 0 hits in the working tree (481 text files) and at HEAD (480). The base had the pair plus the multi-word given name in 4 files. The six scrubbed files still parse as JSON. None of the 48 tokens the scrub added is a real name word. No tracked line lists 4 or more real given names. privacy-audit.json correctly lists the refs that still hold data: origin/main, origin/codex/0.3.0 and v0.2.0, among others. docs/post-mvp/0_3_0_QUESTIONS.md records that the owner deferred any history or tag rewrite. This is not an S4 blocker, but it remains an open privacy exposure for the owner to decide on.

importantFindings.title: Eraser residuals are disclosed and point toward review, not silence
importantFindings.finding: Synthetic probes on the round-3 eraser: touching 3 px strokes of 30, 45, 60 and 90 rows lose only the touching column (2/3 of the ink kept) and the rule is fully erased. A 1 px touching stroke is still lost (disclosed). A touching stroke taller than 120 rows is itself treated as a rule (not a realistic letter height). A rule within 10 px of the image edge, or broken by a wide blob, is left partly unerased. That points toward flags, not toward silent errors.

qolFindings.title: Unflagged staff dates on perturbed sample 4
qolFindings.finding: With erasure, sample 4 rotated −1° or with a 2% inset crop matches 4 unflagged staff dates to missing students' rows. All of those rows are held by the name gate and none is ready. The OCR-level loss and the retake-warning effect are recorded; the matrix could also name the date effect.

qolFindings.title: Near-matches in two fictional files look coincidental
qolFindings.finding: A per-token scan within one edit of a real surname word finds one token in .evidence/C1/summary-preview-13.svg and one in docs/post-mvp/mockups/mock.js. Both predate S4, both files are fictional mock-ups, and neither token sits beside the same student's given name. No action needed unless the owner wants a stricter policy.
